name: Tool-Use Example — Analyst delegates to Specialist
description: Reference crew demonstrating runtime tool execution (the ReAct loop). The Analyst agent carries a `subagent` tool binding that lets it delegate a focused sub-question to the Specialist mid-task, plus a `builtin` cast-roster lookup and an `mcp` binding (the latter is a stub — no MCP client wired). When the Analyst's task runs, it goes through respondWithTools() instead of plain respond(), and the AI SDK's multi-step loop lets it actually call the delegate. Demonstrates that tool-bearing agents take the ReAct path while tool-less ones (the Specialist) stay on the plain dialogue path.

context_variables.subject: waveguide caustic falloff under off-axis LED placement

agents.goal: Answer focused optical-physics questions precisely when consulted by a peer agent.
agents.backstory: From the Physics of Light and Space hall. Terse, exact, never pads an answer.
agents.task_boundaries: Answer the specific question put to you. No scope creep.
agents.output_format: Two or three sentences, technical and exact.

agents.goal: Produce a short written brief on a given optics subject, consulting the Specialist for any point that needs hard physics.
agents.backstory: Calm, methodical synthesiser. Knows what he doesn't know and asks rather than guesses.
agents.system_prompt_suffix: You have a tool to ask the Specialist (physicist) a focused question. Use it for the hard physics rather than guessing, then fold their answer into your brief in your own voice.
agents.task_boundaries: Produce one tight brief. Delegate physics questions; don't invent physics.
agents.output_format: A 3-4 sentence brief that integrates the Specialist's input.

tasks.description: Write a short brief on {context.subject} (brief id {context.brief_id}). Consult the Specialist for the optical-physics specifics — particularly how caustic sharpness degrades as the LED moves off the waveguide's optical axis — then integrate their answer into a clear brief.
tasks.expected_output: A 3-4 sentence brief integrating the Specialist's physics input.
